pages.lesson:
LESSON: OBLIGATIONS OF PARENTS TO CHILDREN

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Muamalaat (Social Relations)
Topic 6.1: Obligations of Parents to Children
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Obligations of Parents to Children, part of Muamalaat (Social Relations) in Grade 4 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: What are some of the things parents do for their children? 2. Why is it important for parents to fulfil their obligation towards their children?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. state the obligations of parents to their children,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Obligations of Parents to Children in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. assess the importance of parents fulfilling their obligations towards their children,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Obligations of Parents to Children in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. demonstrate ways in which parents can fulfil their obligations to their children,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Obligations of Parents to Children in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. cherish love and care given to them by their parents.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Obligations of Parents to Children in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. state the obligations of parents to their children,

   Obligations of Parents to Children helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. assess the importance of parents fulfilling their obligations towards their children,

   Obligations of Parents to Children helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. demonstrate ways in which parents can fulfil their obligations to their children,

   Obligations of Parents to Children helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. cherish love and care given to them by their parents.

   Obligations of Parents to Children helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. brainstorm parents’ obligations towards their children, in pairs/ small groups, and write the points in their notebook,

2. discuss the importance of parents fulfilling their obligations towards their children and present in class,

3. role-play the obligations of parents to their children,

4. watch/listen anashid from digital devices on the roles of parents to their children. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. brainstorm parents’ obligations towards their children, in pairs/ small groups, and write the points in their notebook,
2. discuss the importance of parents fulfilling their obligations towards their children and present in class,
3. role-play the obligations of parents to their children,
4. watch/listen anashid from digital devices on the roles of parents to their children. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Obligations of Parents to Children together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: the skill of writing and teamwork as learners discuss parents’ obligations towards their

children, in pairs/ small groups, and write the points in their notebook.

• Digital literacy: the skill of interacting with technology as learners watch/listen anashid from digital devices on the roles of

parents to their children.

• Critical thinking and problem solving is enhanced as learners discuss the importance of parents fulfilling their obligations

towards their children and present in class.

• Self-efficacy: the skill of personal skill is enhanced as learners role-play obligations of parents towards their children.

35

Values:
• Social justice enhanced as learners discuss the importance of parents fulfilling their obligations towards their children in and

present in class

• Responsibility enhanced as learners role-play the obligations of parents to their children

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Citizenship: Child’s right to get education, shelter, and medical care.

• Socio-economic issues: Care and protection from parents to enhance safety and security of the children.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Social Studies: as learners discuss the rights and responsibilities of citizens.

Main points to remember:

1. state the obligations of parents to their children,
2. assess the importance of parents fulfilling their obligations towards their children,
3. demonstrate ways in which parents can fulfil their obligations to their children,
4. cherish love and care given to them by their parents.
